traces.notes:
Method: read every client query string for the heavy predicates (grep -n on index.html), the full DDL for the core tables in sql/schema.sql, every CREATE INDEX / UNIQUE / FK across sql/*.sql, the trigger bodies, and the sb.js login path. Cannot connect to the live DB, so row counts and the index state of out-of-repo tables are assumptions (flagged per finding). The prepared index_inventory.txt (28 entries) undercounts: my grep finds ~55 CREATE INDEX statements in sql/ (it missed e.g. audit_log_at_idx, audit_log_row_idx, lead_stage_events_to_idx, promotion_requests_lead_idx, idx_quote_quotes_deal/status, idx_system_user_branches_user); the findings above use the corrected inventory.

Already covered — no new index needed (say so explicitly): revenue_streams (UNIQUE(deal_id,stream_type) serves deal_id=eq/in at 9385, 9445, 9530, 11805, 12664, 12707, 13710); revenue_stream_months (UNIQUE(stream_id,month) serves stream_id=eq/in, stream_id+month=eq at 9397, and the PostgREST resource-embed join from revenue_streams at 11805/12664/12707/13574); engagement_people, deal_collaborators, deal_contacts/opportunity_contacts, home_organisation_members (UNIQUE pairs with the queried column leading); promotion_requests (lead_idx, status_idx, partial unique pending); lead_stage_events ((to_status,at) serves the report at 24458); lead_contacts, lead_description_log, campaign_targets, campaign_cadence_steps, secured_snapshots, system_user_regions/branches, quote_* tables.

revenue_stream_months.month is TEXT, but every writer formats it zero-padded 'YYYY-MM' (index.html:9589 `${d0.getFullYear()}-${String(d0.getMonth()+1).padStart(2,'0')}` and 22773-22776 monthStr) so `order=month.asc` (9450, 9535) and text comparisons sort chronologically; no functional index or type change is needed. Do not add a plain (month) index — the only month predicate (9397) is always combined with stream_id and is already covered.

Small lookups (<100-500 rows: regions, branches, stages, stage_categories, service_major, service_sub, lead_sources, activity_types, next_actions, dmu_roles, roles, permissions, role_permissions, user_roles, system_users, system_user_regions/branches, user_permission_overrides, home_organisation_members, milestone_types/groups, work_projects, decline_reasons, red_flags, strategic_decisions, qualification_dimensions, settings, broadcasts, user_presence, bug_reports, research_campaigns, sales_campaigns, industry_sectors) need no indexes — their `active=eq` / `order=name` predicates are microseconds; their cost is purely the round trip.

Free-text search: the client does NO server-side ilike/text search on people/organisations/leads (grep for 'ilike' in index.html returns nothing; all list filtering is client-side over allData), so no pg_trgm GIN index is warranted today. If a server-side search is introduced later, add `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm` and GIN(trgm) on organisations.name / people.first_name||last_name at that point.

Trigger interplay worth knowing for the other slices: the audit trigger (add_audit_log.sql) adds one audit_log INSERT + index maintenance to every row write on 17 tables (including bulk revenue_stream_months POSTs at 9594/22781 and each 150-row PATCH at 16790), and refresh_lead_next_action rewrites the leads row (another audit row + idx_leads_next_action_date churn) on every engagement write for a lead. The index changes above keep audit_log's index count at 4 (net +1) deliberately.

Honest sizing: with tables in the low thousands of rows, each seq scan is ~1-15 ms against a ~1.4 s proxied round trip, so the user-felt gain from this slice alone is small today; it becomes material for engagements/audit_log as they grow and is decisive for the O(N x M) cascade-delete cases. The round-trip count/sequencing (other slices) is the dominant lever.

traces.notes: Assumptions and verification needed (no live DB access): (1) The live DB carries objects not in sql/: a trigger stamping leads.first_engaged_at (index.html:23515 comment) and, per round-1 LI-3, one maintaining last_touch_date; the DDL for sites, deal_contacts, engagement_milestones, lead_service_estimates, user_presence, broadcasts, work_projects (referenced migrations add_broadcasts.sql / add_engagement_milestones.sql are absent). Before changing any trigger run `select tgrelid::regclass, tgname, pg_get_triggerdef(oid) from pg_trigger where not tgisinternal order by 1,2;` and `select conrelid::regclass, conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) from pg_constraint where contype = 'f';` and check the SRV-4/SRV-7 embeddings against that FK list. (2) leads_status_check in schema.sql:1210-ish only allows New/Working/Qualified/Promoted/Dormant/Dead while the app writes Hold/Nurture — it must have been relaxed in an un-versioned migration; sweep_leads() relies on that. (3) Volumes (audit_log growth, leads/engagements counts) are estimates; the trigger CPU numbers are order-of-magnitude. (4) Proxy: sb.js:253 rewrites /.netlify/functions/sb/<anything> to /rest/v1/<anything>, so /sb/rpc/<fn> reaches /rest/v1/rpc/<fn> unchanged; Prefer is forwarded (sb.js:293); x-actor-id is forwarded so audit attribution survives inside RPCs (the header GUC is visible to triggers called from the function). Client caveat: api() at index.html:2040-2044 refuses non-GET for read-only users unless the 'table' is in READ_ONLY_WRITE_ALLOW — call read RPCs with GET (STABLE functions) and add the write RPCs ('rpc/sweep_leads', 'rpc/promote_lead', 'rpc/merge_organisations') to that list only if read-only users should reach them (they should not). GET RPCs also get the 3-attempt retry (1991-1992). (5) Grant `execute` on each function and `select` on each view to service_role (the proxy's key) — anon/authenticated grants are unnecessary while only the proxy talks to PostgREST. (6) Deliberately not repeated from round 1: F7 (heartbeat polling — a `heartbeat(p_person_id, p_version)` RPC doing the user_presence upsert and returning live broadcasts would make it 1 hop/min instead of 2-3, needs a unique key on user_presence.person_id), LR-06 (leads_register view — same pattern as SRV-2), PW-08/LI-4 (_liSyncMilestones per-checkbox writes: engagement_milestones is NOT audited and has no triggers, so a single array POST with on_conflict=engagement_id,milestone_type_id is purely a client change), EH-2 (bulk shift RPC — TRG-A1/A2 quantify its DB side). (7) _liSyncMilestones, lead_service_estimates, lead_stage_requests, promotion_requests-per-row writes are cheap on the DB side (no triggers beyond audit where listed); their cost is round trips only. (8) Order of value: SRV-6 + SRV-3 + TRG-A3 fix the login-to-dashboard path (~22 sequential hops today); SRV-9 + SRV-5 + TRG-A2 fix the three heaviest writes; SRV-1/2/7 fix the register-style pages; TRG-A1/A4 are hygiene that pays off once bulk statements replace the per-row loops.
